resources.string: Elamon shows a computer\'s load, temperatures, memory, processes and monitors live, and controls its links, media and power. The computer runs a small service, elamond, that only paired phones can reach.
Install the Elamon service, elamond, on the computer (Linux). In a terminal there, as yourself, not root:
It installs elamond and starts it. Then run as root the commands it prints. On NixOS, use the module instead: Step-by-step guide below.
Run this on the computer. It shows a QR code and a six-digit code:
Point this phone\'s camera at the QR code, or tap Add computer and enter the code.
The easiest way: run elamond pair on the computer and point the phone\'s camera at the QR code it shows.
Or enter the computer\'s address, then the six-digit code.
Check that these digits match the certificate line elamond pair shows on the computer:
Six digits shown by elamond pair
A link asks to pair with %1$s. Pair only if you just ran elamond pair there.
elamond pair asks there whether to allow this phone.
The computer didn\'t allow this phone. Run elamond pair again and answer y.
The computer has as many phones paired as it takes. Revoke one there with elamond revoke, then pair again.
The computer gave an id this app doesn\'t take. Check that it is your computer and that its elamond is up to date.
The computer answered as another computer than the one it said it was, so nothing was saved.
The computer doesn\'t answer. Check that the Elamon service is running and that the phone is on the same network or VPN.
Something answered at this address, but not with the certificate the computer announced. Pairing was stopped to be safe.
Wrong code. After five wrong codes the computer needs a new one.
Too many wrong codes from this phone. Start elamond pair again for a new code.
The computer isn\'t waiting for a phone. Run elamond pair on it first.
The computer paired this phone, but the phone\'s key store couldn\'t keep the key safe, so nothing was saved. Try again; elamond revoke on the computer removes the pairing left unused.
The computer paired this phone, but the phone couldn\'t save the pairing, so nothing was kept. Try again; elamond revoke on the computer removes the pairing left unused.
The computer paired this phone again, but the phone couldn\'t keep the new key, and the pairing it had before has ended with it. Run elamond pair on the computer again and pair once more.
The computer stopped answering. If it let this phone in already, the pairing it had before ended with it: run elamond pair on the computer again and pair once more.
This pairing code is from a newer elamond than this app reads. Update the app, then scan it again.
This pairing link is incomplete or damaged. Run elamond pair on the computer and scan the new code.
This phone will stop showing it, and the computer will be asked to remove this phone too. To see it again, pair again: elamond pair offers this phone its profile back.
The computer couldn\'t be told. To remove this phone there, run elamond revoke on it (elamond clients lists the phones).
The computer no longer accepts it, maybe after elamond revoke. Run elamond pair on the computer and pair again.

This phone can no longer read its key for the computer, as happens when the phone\'s key store was reset. Run elamond pair on the computer and pair again; elamond revoke there removes the old pairing.
This happens when the Elamon service\'s data was reset or reinstalled, but also when something else pretends to be the computer. If you didn\'t reset it, check your network before pairing again.
The computer may be off or asleep, the Elamon service not running, or the phone on another network. Elamon keeps trying.

This phone\'s role or profile on %1$s shows none of its dashboards. On the computer, elamond clients lists the phones with their IDs; elamond clients role or elamond clients profile changes what this one sees.
The computer turned this phone away
This computer\'s Elamon service is newer than this app. Update Elamon to see everything it sends.
This computer runs elamond %1$s. Update it to %2$s or newer: some readings need it.
sees the basics only: load, memory, temperatures, disks, network and battery
may also start and stop the links\' units, play media, set the power profile and run actions
may do everything, power and ending processes included
It\'s asked to close, the way a window\'s close button would. Most programs save and exit.
It ends at once, without saving anything.
This computer only lets the app watch. To also control power, links, processes and media from here, turn it on in the service\'s settings:
in ~/.config/elamon/elamond.toml, or services.elamond.settings.control = true on NixOS.
Only web pages (http or https) are opened from the app.
Every session of this user is locked.
Elamon loses the connection until the computer wakes up.
Unsaved work in open programs is lost.
Unsaved work is lost, and only someone at the computer can turn it back on.
This phone has no screen lock, so Elamon can\'t ask to unlock it first. Set one in the phone\'s settings to be asked.

Elamon has two parts: this app, and elamond, a small service on the computer you want to watch. It needs no root and runs as your user. Everything is set on the computer; the app only draws what the service describes.
On NixOS, use the module instead. Add the project to your flake\'s inputs:
Import its module and turn the service on. openFirewall opens the ports; linger keeps the service running while you\'re logged out. For Home Manager, see the full guide.
One command installs the service for your user (run it as yourself, not root) and runs elamond setup, which prints the few commands that need root:
On NixOS, the openFirewall option above does it. Without it:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. Otherwise open TCP %1$s (the service) and UDP %2$s (mDNS, so the app can find the computer on the local network) in the one you use.
It shows a QR code and a six-digit code, good for five minutes. Scan the QR code with the phone\'s camera and open the link: that pairs in one tap.

Or in this app tap the computer under Found on this network, or Add computer and its address, and enter the code. Check that the certificate digits the app shows match the Certificate line on the computer.
Then elamond pair asks on the computer: Allow? [y/N]. Answer y if the phone is yours, and keep elamond pair running until the phone is paired.
Settings, dashboards, the control panel, roles, backups and troubleshooting are in the full guide, online.
